parsed.explanation: A self-governing territory with no trans-specific criminal offence, a goods-and-services discrimination ban covering gender reassignment in force since 2007, trans-inclusive hate-crime and hate-speech coverage enacted July 2026, a conversion-therapy offence, and a supreme court with a record of striking down discriminatory law (2011 age of consent, 2013 adoption). No documented border refusals, police targeting, facility bans, custody mistreatment or trans-specific violence. The negatives are lighter-weight: no legal gender-recognition route (a resident-facing gap that nonetheless fixes the marker a visitor is read under), an unestablished question whether the governing state's equality act or 2025 single-sex-services code extends here, and no sourcing on how the 2026 hate-crime amendment operates in practice. Documented protection without documented enforcement outcomes, and no operating oversight body, holds it below the acceptance-with-working-remedies tier.

entry_documents.exposure: No local gender-recognition route; the dossier states a trans visitor is read at the border and in public under an unalterable marker. No documented refusal of entry, secondary screening or document-mismatch detention.
entry_documents.protection: No border-specific protection documented. The 2006 equal opportunities act covers goods and services, not immigration practice.
entry_documents.interaction: The gap is the absence of local recognition machinery rather than a documented visitor-facing border rule; the governing state's equality act and 2025 single-sex-services code are not established as extended.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No trans-specific custody, placement or interrogation practice appears in the dossier.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No record of how a document discrepancy at the border would escalate into investigation or detention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. The jurisdiction is a single legal unit with no internal regional tier; no facility-access restriction is recorded.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The governing state's single-sex-services code binds only if extended by order, and no extension appears; the dossier therefore records no operative facility exclusion.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No denial of care, ward-placement rule or medication seizure is recorded.
care_services.protection: Conversion-therapy offence enacted July 2026; discrimination in provision of goods and services prohibited since 2007.
care_services.interaction: The conversion-therapy offence is stated generally; whether it covers transgender identity or only sexual orientation is unsourced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No law criminalises gender expression or presentation; no state threat-framing of trans people is recorded.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: July 2026 amendments extend hate-crime and hate-speech protection to transgender identity; gender reassignment is a protected ground under the 2007-in-force equal opportunities act.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: No enforcement data on the 2013 or 2026 hate-crime provisions appears, so practical operation of the trans-inclusive amendment is unverified.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No minor-specific trans rule, school-placement or parental-consent barrier is recorded.
minors_guardians.protection: Gender-neutral age of consent of 16 since 2012; adoption expressly open to same-sex couples from April 2024.
minors_guardians.interaction: Nothing in the dossier indicates a guardian travelling with a trans minor faces a distinct facility, care or documentation exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence, extortion, app-ambush or police harassment is recorded in the sourced material.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime coverage extended to transgender identity July 2026; a supreme court that has struck down discriminatory provisions.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of incidents in a jurisdiction that produces legislative and judicial records is a mildly positive signal, but no prosecution or complaint outcome is sourced.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No documented trans-specific remedy outcome; the medicalised 'gender reassignment' definition may not reach all trans visitors.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Statutory goods-and-services protection since 1 March 2007; courts have invalidated discriminatory law on age of consent (2011) and adoption (2013).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Rule of law operates in this field, but whether it operates for trans visitors specifically is unsourced; no oversight body or compensation record appears.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra has a documented, routinely enforced visitor-exclusion register barring trans travellers at the border. Here no border bar, refusal or exclusion practice is recorded at all, and discrimination in services is prohibited by statute. Far above 0.35.

Kestrel Isles documents secondary screening, refused admission on discretionary public-order grounds and humiliating searches of trans visitors. This dossier records no such screening pattern and adds an operative anti-discrimination statute, so it sits materially above 0.55.

Meridia documents border-officer training and a civil-liberties tribunal producing release and compensation. This jurisdiction has comparable entry legality and stronger statutory protection but no documented border practice, no tribunal remedy and no compensation record, so it sits slightly below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a self-governing territory whose own parliament and courts govern the visitor's whole journey: entry, services, hate crime and care are all local, and no regional tier or applied parent code is documented. Documented positives are real and statute-based — a goods-and-services ban on gender-reassignment discrimination in force since 2007, trans-inclusive hate-crime coverage and a conversion-therapy offence both enacted July 2026, and a supreme court that has struck down discriminatory law. Documented negatives are thinner: no gender-recognition route, so the marker a visitor is read under is fixed, and no sourced evidence of how the 2026 trans-inclusive provisions are enforced. The unresolved question of whether the governing state's equality act or single-sex-services code extends here is an open question, not a documented exposure. No criminalisation, no documented targeting, no facility or custody rule: the traveller's exposure is everyday discretion and friction, not state threat.
